newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS upgrades Four Seasons notes.
newsitem.headline: DBRS upgrades Four Seasons notes.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service on Monday raised the rating on the unsecured notes of Four Seasons Hotels to BBB (low) from BB (high) with a stable trend.

The Toronto-based bond rating agency said the upgrade reflects the company's transformation from essentially the ownership of luxury hotels to the management of luxury hotels and resorts around the world. The upgrade also reflects the elimination of a substantial amount of debt from its balance sheet, DBRS said.
The company's association with Prince Alwaleed of Saudi Arabia also offer substantial growth opportunities around to world to gain new hotel management contracts, DBRS said.

DBRS said challenges facing the company include the inherent cyclicality of the hospitality industry, the intense competition in the luxury hotel industry, and the potential loss of the highly profitable management contract of the Regent Hong Kong in 2000.
